subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: May synchronous exec authorization intentionally read the previous complete policy while a same-process async policy write is in progress, or must every authorization remain serialized with that write?
rationale: Atomic rename guarantees a structurally complete file but does not decide the authorization-freshness contract; accepting a stale policy window could permit execution after an administrator has initiated a revocation or tightening.

options.title: Preserve policy serialization
options.body: Refactor the nested call path to reuse the writer's locked snapshot or a shared process-local lock without performing an unlocked authorization read.

options.title: Permit bounded stale reads
options.body: Explicitly approve the previous-policy window, document its security semantics, and add live and regression proof covering concurrent revocation behavior.

recommendation.title: Preserve policy serialization
recommendation.body: Refactor the nested call path to reuse the writer's locked snapshot or a shared process-local lock without performing an unlocked authorization read.

likelyOwner.reason: The current serialization and fail-closed contract was introduced through their merged exec-approval race hardening work.
